text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- The Norwegian Trade and Industry Confederation sees a rise in prices below two percent in 1997. The Confederation's estimate is considerably lower than the inflation forecasts from the government (2.5 percent), the central bank (2.5 percent) and the statistics office (2.3 percent).
- Shipping company Anders Wilhelmsen & Co may reduce the company's share in Royal Caribbean Cruise Line. Wilhelmsen has 39 percent of the shares in RCCL and is the largest shareholder in RCCL.

- Only 23 of 176 electricity utilities want to compete for households customers. One of the purposes of the deregulation of the electricity market in 1991 was to establish competition for household customers among electricity utilities.

- During the last two weeks travel agencies have moved five percent of Scandinavian Airlines System's (SAS) passengers to other airlines. The travel agencies are protesting against SAS cutting the agencies' commissions.

- Norway's emission of smog-creating substances is 24 percent higher than earlier believed. It is becoming increasingly difficult for Norway to meet an international obligation to decrease emissions by 30 percent.
